tools.name: about_this_server
tools.description: What this MCP server is, what each access tier includes, and how to obtain access. Call this first if you are unsure what the server offers, or after any tool refuses you — the refusal names a tier, and this tool explains what that tier costs and what it adds. Requires no credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_instruments" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Find EU legislation and UK legislation by keyword, acronym (GDPR, DORA, AIA), the common name practitioners use ('Market Abuse Regulation', 'MLRs', 'UK GDPR'), …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_legislation · Private data: about_this_server, search_instruments, get_legislation · Public sink: search_instruments.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_legislation · Private data: about_this_server, search_instruments, get_legislation · Public sink: search_instruments

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
